transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Morris (Redwood AE), Khalid Rahman (Redwood CSM), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Pegasus VP Product), Omar Singh (Pegasus Head of ML), Priya Patel (Pegasus SRE), Evan Moore (Pegasus Finance)

Summary (auto): Quarterly health check focusing on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment for personalization and search. Customer open to dedicated capacity discussion if cost/latency ROI meets threshold. Agreed to run a 2-hour benchmark next week focusing on tail latency and KV cache warmup.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jenna: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR. I'll kick off, I'm Jenna from Redwood, joined by Khalid and Diego.
[00:08] Laura: Thanks, Jenna. Appreciate you fitting this in, we know end of quarter is busy.
[00:12] Khalid: Yep, quick agenda: usage & cost trends, reliability incidents since last QBR, roadmap asks, and then next steps.
[00:20] Omar: Sounds good. We'll focus on the personalization pipeline first - that's where most of our spend is.
[00:25] Diego: Quick note, I'll share a perf slide - but the concrete thing is we want to look at tail latency on the 8k prompt flows and how KV cache warmup behaves during bursts.
[00:35] Priya: For SRE, main concern is the two outages in May - one was a region failover, one was a spike due to a cache eviction. We're trying to understand mitigation.
[00:45] Jenna: Right, on outages: we logged an incident 2026-05-14 for the region failover, and another transient on 2026-05-22 tied to aggressive cache TTL on your end. Diego, can you recap cause?
[00:55] Diego: Yeah, from the Redwood side the 05-14 event was a provider region network flap that triggered our smart routing; some requests fell back to a lower capacity pool which increased latency briefly. We have the trace ids in the console. The 05-22 spike: looks like a large job from Pegasus invalidated prefixes which forced KV repopulation; that caused a short tail increase while the cache warmed.
[01:18] Omar: That matches our logs, we kicked a massive re-index job that week. Can we set guardrails to avoid full prefix invalidation?
[01:25] Khalid: Absolutely, we can suggest a TTL tuning and we can also configure prefix-aware batching so the reindex doesn't blow the cache. We'll put recommendations in the post-call doc.
[01:33] Evan: On cost - finance flagged a 38% increase month-over-month in token spend in May. We need to understand drivers and options.
[01:42] Jenna: We dug into usage: two big drivers - the personalization reranks and a spike from experimentation where a new model variant was rolled to 20% traffic. We can show the per-route token breakdown.
[01:53] Priya: Can you show the route breakdown now or in the dashboard?
[01:56] Diego: I'll screen share the console after, but quick points: rerank route accounts for ~45% of tokens, average prompt length is 1.2k tokens, and the new model variant (quantized 4-bit) has a slightly longer generation length due to system prompts, so token counts rose.
[02:15] Laura: So options would be reduce model size, quantize differently, or change batching?
[02:19] Khalid: Yes - Redwood Optimize suggestions were to increase batching for rerank during off-peak, enable prefix caching for stable prefixes, and consider a lower-capacity variant for low-priority traffic. We'll attach tuning knobs.
[02:30] Omar: We heard about Dedicated capacity - would that help cost predictability here?
[02:34] Jenna: Dedicated helps with predictable throughput and can lower per-token cost if you commit. But you lose a bit of the elastic burst unless you buy burst capacity. We can run a cost model: commit level vs per-token baseline.
[02:45] Evan: We need a model showing 3 scenarios: stay hosted, commit to Dedicated mid-size, or hybrid (dedicated for live, hosted for experiments).
[02:53] Jenna: We'll produce that. Evan, is there a target ROI or payback window you need?
[02:57] Evan: Finance wants <9 months payback on infra changes.
[03:01] Khalid: Good to know. We'll include that in the model.
[03:05] Priya: On security/compliance, Pegasus needs SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs for legal. Are those available?
[03:12] Jenna: Yes, we have SOC 2 and ISO links - I'll share the artifacts. Also note KMS integration for customer-managed keys is supported for Private deployments.
[03:22] Laura: We're evaluating Private for data residency but it's a big lift. Could we simulate with VPC first?
[03:27] Diego: VPC peering is supported; for true on-prem we'll need an additional package. For most customers, the VPC option plus dedicated compute hits most requirements.
[03:36] Omar: Performance question - tail latency under peak. In our load tests last month, p95 was fine but p99 spiked.
[03:43] Diego: That's usually KV cache cold starts and also the batching window. Two mitigations: keep KV warm via periodic warmers and reduce max batching latency for critical routes. We can instrument a heatmap for p50/p95/p99 per route.
[03:55] Priya: Can we get an alert for p99 crossing threshold?
[03:58] Khalid: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-route alerts; we'll set that up and push thresholds to your PagerDuty.
[04:05] Laura: Roadmap ask: better observability on prompt tokens and rollbacks during model rollouts. We had a bad rollout in April.
[04:12] Jenna: Rollouts can do canary and automatic rollback on quality regressions; sounds like we should review your rollout policy and attach a kpi (e.g., NDCG drop) as a trigger.
[04:21] Omar: Also want to run a full benchmark for the 8k flows - can Redwood run it with us?
[04:25] Diego: Yes, we'll run a controlled benchmark. We need: sample prompts, target concurrency, and access to the staging dataset. Khalid, can you coordinate?
[04:33] Khalid: Will do. I'll reach out to Priya to schedule a 2-hour window next week.
[04:38] Priya: Prefer Tue AM (PDT).
[04:40] Khalid: Noted.
[04:42] Evan: Any legal/pricing paperwork to move to Dedicated?
[04:45] Jenna: We can prepare a contract amendment PDF with tiered commit options. I'll include finance-friendly language and a migration plan.
[04:53] Laura: Great. Last, success metrics for next quarter - what should we track?
[04:57] Khalid: Proposed: 1) reduce token spend variance to <10% month-over-month, 2) p99 latency under 800ms for personalization during peak, 3) zero production incidents from cache evictions, 4) measurable model quality stable within +/-2% on eval set.
[05:14] Omar: Those seem reasonable.
[05:16] Jenna: OK let's recap next steps.
[05:18] Jenna: Action items: Jenna will send the cost breakdown and contract options by Friday; Khalid will schedule benchmark and set up alerts; Diego will prepare TTL and prefix caching recommendations; Priya/Evan will confirm budget timeline.
[05:30] Laura: Thanks, team. Appreciate the partnership.
[05:33] Jenna: Thanks all, I'll follow up in the doc and set a meeting invite for the benchmark.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hears ("K V cash" heard in raw transcript) and speaker overlaps. Shared artifacts referenced: link: console.redwood.ai/pegasus/usage-2026-05 (dashboard), link: drive.redwood.ai/soc2-iso (security pack), link: drive.redwood.ai/qbr/pegasus-2026-06 (QBR slides).

End of transcript.
